data.name: Sample - CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian - 1.0.0
data.description: Sample playbooks for the "CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian" connector. If you are planning to use any of the sample playbooks in your environment, ensure that you clone those playbooks and move them to a different collection, since the sample playbook collection gets deleted during connector upgrade and delete.

workflows.name: Investigate AI Agent
workflows.description: Investigate one AI agent: the agent record, recent sessions for its product, and ThreatGraph session activity for those sessions.

routes.name: Get AI Agent -> List AI Agent Sessions
List AI Agent Sessions -> Sessions Found

groups.name: Note: Agent Found
groups.description:
The rest of the chain keys off the first agent the query returns. A
quiet fleet (nothing seen in the window) ends the run here instead of
failing on the required agent id.

groups.name: Note: Get AI Agent
groups.description:
Wired to the first agent from List AI Agents. get_ai_agent wants the
opaque AIAgent Id, not the 32-hex sensor id -- clone this playbook and
pin the id to a specific agent for a repeatable investigation.

groups.name: Note: List AI Agent Sessions
groups.description:
Scoped to the agent's product, not the agent itself: the session store
has no per-agent server-side filter, so the product tag is the
narrowest scope the API offers.

groups.name: Note: Get Session Activity
groups.description:
ThreatGraph activity (tools, models, processes, MCP servers as edges)
for every session listed above. get_session_activity accepts session
UUIDs or full vertex keys and resolves either.

workflows.name: Investigate AI Detections
workflows.description: Pull AI-agent detections in the lookback window and the per-agent score rollup beside them.

routes.name: List AI Detections -> Get Detection Scores

groups.name: Note: Get Detection Scores
groups.description:
The per-agent maximum detection score over the same window -- the quick
"which hosts are burning" view next to the raw detections.

workflows.name: Report Fleet Inventory
workflows.description: One-call environment summary: agents, sessions, tools and skills grouped by product or name, plus the detection rollup.

workflows.name: Report Agent Tool Usage
workflows.description: Recent AI tool invocations from LogScale and the invocation counts beside them. Tool-usage events only reach back 7 days and default to a 2-hour window.

routes.name: List Tool Usage -> Get Tool Usage Counts

workflows.name: >> CrowdStrike Guardian > Init Macros
workflows.description: Creates the Guardian last-pull-time macro if it does not already exist. Called by Fetch during the wizard's environment-setup pass.

routes.name: Get Guardian Macros -> Guardian Macro Exists
Guardian Macro Exists -> Create Guardian Macro
routes.label: Not Exist

routes.name: Guardian Macro Exists -> Fetch Macro Current Value
routes.label: Exist

routes.name: Fetch Macro Current Value -> Update Macro If Required

workflows.name: > CrowdStrike Guardian > Fetch
workflows.description: Reads the last-pull-time watermark, turns it into a detections lookback window, fetches Guardian detections since then, and maps them to FortiSOAR alert shape.

arguments.fetch_window: {%- set macro = vars.steps.Get_Macro_Value.data['hydra:member'] -%} {%- if not macro or macro[0].value == '0' or vars.request.env_setup -%} {{ vars.cold_start_hours }}h {%- else -%} {%- set hours = ((arrow.utcnow() - arrow.get(macro[0].value)).total_seconds() / 3600) | round(0, 'ceil') | int -%} {%- if hours < 1 %}1h{% elif hours > 2160 %}2160h{% else %}{{ hours }}h{% endif -%} {%- endif -%}

arguments.name: CrowdStrike Falcon Guardian

routes.name: Set Time Configuration -> Set Fetch Window

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
Wizard-editable defaults. `cold_start_hours` is the lookback used the
first time this ingestion runs (macro still '0'); after that the
watermark sets the window. The macro name is scoped to this playbook's
UUID so two ingestion configurations never share a watermark.

groups.name: Note: Environment Setup
groups.description:
Runs when the watermark macro does not exist yet -- not only on the
wizard's `vars.request.env_setup` first pass.

Keying solely off env_setup left ingestion permanently broken whenever
the macro was missing: `Update Last Alert Pull Time` only *updates*, it
does not create, so every run cold-started at the configured lookback
and the watermark was never written. A silent failure, because nothing
errors.

This step must therefore come AFTER Get Macro Value, so its absence can
be seen. The macro is primed to '0', which Set Fetch Window reads as
"cold start" for this one run.

groups.name: Note: Set Time Configuration
groups.description:
`curr_timestamp` is captured before the fetch and only written back to
the macro after Ingest succeeds, so a failed run re-pulls its window
instead of silently skipping it.

groups.name: Note: Set Fetch Window
groups.description:
The detections API takes a relative lookback, not a from/to pair, so
the watermark becomes a window: cold start uses the wizard's lookback;
afterwards the window is the hours elapsed since the last pull, rounded
up and clamped to 1..2160 (2160h = 90d, the detections route's
ceiling). A window narrower than one hour is bumped to 1h so back-to-
back runs still see the records they could otherwise straddle.

groups.name: Note: Save Result
groups.description:
The Fetch -> Ingest contract. Ingest reads every one of these back off
the workflow_reference step ("List Detections") as
`vars.steps.List_Detections.<key>`.

workflows.name: CrowdStrike Guardian > Ingest
workflows.description: Orchestrator: calls Fetch, then either returns a sample record for the wizard's Data Mapping preview (env_setup mode) or creates the alerts and advances the last-pull-time watermark.

routes.name: Create Record -> Update Last Alert Pull Time

groups.name: Note: Mapping Preview
groups.description:
The Data Ingestion Wizard runs the Ingest playbook with
`vars.request.env_setup == true` while the analyst designs the field
mapping in the UI. In that mode we return the first fetched,
already-mapped detection so the wizard can render the Data Mapping
preview with real alert fields -- no alerts are written. `false` (or
missing) is the real ingestion path.

groups.name: Note: Return Sample
groups.description:
The sample for the wizard's Data Mapping preview.
`vars.steps.List_Detections.data.alerts[0]` is the first mapped
detection from the Fetch window; its keys are the alert field names
`field_mapping.map_detection_to_alert` emits (external_id, name,
severity, alert_state, alert_generation_epoch, ...), which the wizard
maps onto the alerts module. Falls back to a representative hardcoded
record when the window is empty so the preview still renders.

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
Severity/status/type maps are keyed on the values `field_mapping.py`
emits and cover every one of them -- an unmapped value would make
`resolveRange` miss and the alert POST fail with a picklist 400.
`field_mapping` resolves severity to the five FortiSOAR severity labels
and alert_state to New/Open/Closed, so the two lists have to be changed
together.

The type map sends Guardian's fixed alert_type label ("CrowdStrike
Guardian") to the AlertType picklist value "Other / Unknown": the label
is not a member of the stock picklist, and the alert's identity rides
on source, name and description instead.

groups.name: Note: Create Record
groups.description:
`is_upsert` routes this at /api/3/upsert/alerts, keyed on `sourceId`, so a
re-ingest updates the existing alert. Without it the plain insert path
409s on the sourceid uniqueness constraint the moment a window overlaps a
previous run -- which every incremental pull does.

groups.name: Note: Update Last Alert Pull Time
groups.description:
Advances the watermark only after the alerts are written, so a failed
Create Record leaves the window to be retried.
